title: AWA Communication Technologies Museum
raw_text:
AWA Communication Technologies Museum

"200 Years of Innovations"

Put away the cell phones and iPads and tune into cutting edge times of yore when famous inventors such as Guglielmo Marconi, Samuel Morse, Edwin Armstrong and other communication pioneers were at their peak. Experience 200 years of communication technologies. See a wide range of history such as the first transistor radio, the first cell phone, hear a thundering 1000 watt spark transmitter, wonder at the Voice of America station from Delano, California, see the Titanic Wireless Room, see and listen to a working Western Union office, walk into a 1925 Radio Store, see shelf after shelf of radios and televisions, and much, much more!

AWA Communication Technologies Museum is sponsored by the Antique Wireless Association and its 1400 international members. Begun in 1952, the Museum is located on a four building, five acre campus in Bloomfield, NY, a short drive  southeast of Rochester.

Recognized world-wide as the finest collection of communication artifacts, the Museum provides a rich and unique experience for visitors of ages. Located at 6925 Route 5, Bloomfield, NY, 14469 the Museum is open Tuesdays 10 am to 3 pm and Saturdays 1 pm to 5 pm. We are closed on New Year's Day, Easter, the Fourth of July, and Christmas.

Adult admission is $10; Seniors, Active Service Members and Veterans are $9;  Members, kids and teens are always free.

title: Garth Fagan Dance, Inc.
raw_text:
Garth Fagan Dance, Inc.

50 Chestnut Street, Floor 3 Rochester, NY 14604

Garth Fagan Dance is an internationally acclaimed contemporary dance company founded in 1970 by visionary choreographer and educator Garth Fagan. Based in Rochester, New York, the company is recognized for its distinctive movement vocabulary, Fagan Technique™, which blends elements of modern, post-modern, ballet, and Afro-Caribbean dance into a powerful and innovative artistic form. Through more than five decades of performance, education, and community engagement, Garth Fagan Dance has become one of the most influential and enduring dance organizations in the United States. The company has toured extensively throughout North America, Europe, Asia, Australia, South America, and Africa, earning widespread critical acclaim for its athleticism, musicality, and emotional depth. Garth Fagan’s groundbreaking choreography gained global recognition through his Tony Award-winning work for the Broadway production of *The Lion King*, which continues to inspire audiences worldwide. Beyond performance, Garth Fagan Dance is deeply committed to arts education and cultural enrichment. Through classes, workshops, residencies, and outreach programs, the organization serves students, emerging artists, and community members of all ages and backgrounds. These initiatives foster creativity, discipline, self-expression, and an appreciation for the performing arts. Today, under the artistic leadership of Norwood Pennewell and Natalie Rogers-Cropper, Garth Fagan Dance continues to preserve and advance Garth Fagan’s artistic legacy while cultivating new generations of dancers and audiences. The company remains dedicated to artistic excellence, innovation, and community impact, using dance as a powerful vehicle for storytelling, cultural connection, and human expression. Throughout the year, audiences can engage with Garth Fagan Dance through performances, educational programs, and community events across Rochester, including Juneteenth celebrations, the company’s home season at Nazareth University, productions presented during the ESL Rochester Fringe Festival at the Garth Fagan Dance Studio Theater on Chestnut Street, and much, much, more!
